name: APT29
description: APT29 (Cozy Bear/Midnight Blizzard) is a highly sophisticated Russian state-sponsored threat actor attributed to the SVR (Foreign Intelligence Service). Known for stealthy, long-term intrusions targeting government, diplomatic, defence, and think-tank organisations. Responsible for the SolarWinds Orion supply chain compromise and Microsoft corporate network breach in 2024. Uses bespoke malware families and legitimate cloud services for C2 to evade detection.

name: APT28
description: APT28 (Fancy Bear) is a Russian GRU Unit 26165 threat actor with extensive history of targeting NATO governments, defence contractors, political parties, and critical infrastructure. Known for the DNC hack (2016), WADA anti-doping agency breach, and numerous spear-phishing campaigns using Brute Ratel C4 and X-Agent implants. Highly active in ongoing Ukraine-related cyber operations.

name: Lazarus
description: Lazarus Group (HIDDEN COBRA) is a prolific North Korean state-sponsored threat actor believed to operate under the Reconnaissance General Bureau. Responsible for the 2014 Sony Pictures hack, 2016 Bangladesh Bank heist ($81M theft), 2017 WannaCry ransomware, and ongoing cryptocurrency theft operations totalling over $3 billion. The TraderTraitor sub-cluster targets cryptocurrency exchanges and DeFi platforms through supply chain attacks on developer environments.

name: Volt Typhoon
description: Volt Typhoon is a PRC state-sponsored threat actor with a distinctive focus on LOTL (living-off-the-land) techniques to pre-position within US and allied critical infrastructure — particularly utilities, communications, and transportation sectors. Unlike most APTs, Volt Typhoon avoids deploying malware in favour of native OS tools (netsh, wmic, certutil). CISA, NSA, and FBI issued a joint advisory in 2024 warning of Volt Typhoon's deep persistence in CNI networks, potentially enabling disruption during geopolitical conflict.

name: FIN7
description: FIN7 (Carbon Spider) is a prolific Russia-based cybercriminal group with over a decade of operations targeting the retail, hospitality, and financial sectors. Known for the Carbanak banking malware framework, FIN7 has stolen an estimated $1.2 billion globally. They evolved from point-of-sale malware to sophisticated BEC campaigns, ransomware deployment (partnering with REvil and BlackMatter), and supply chain attacks. Several core members were indicted by the DOJ in 2018 but operations continue.

name: TA505
description: TA505 (Hive0065) is a prolific financially motivated threat actor and one of the most active ransomware operators globally. Operators of the Cl0p ransomware and responsible for massive exploitation of zero-day vulnerabilities in managed file transfer (MFT) platforms including Accellion FTA, GoAnywhere, and MOVEit Transfer. Their exploitation-to-exfiltration timeline is typically under 24 hours. TA505 has victimised over 2,500 organisations worldwide.

name: LockBit
description: LockBit is the world's most prolific ransomware-as-a-service operation, claiming responsibility for over 2,000 victims globally. After Operation Cronos disrupted LockBit 3.0 infrastructure in February 2024, the group re-emerged with LockBit 4.0 featuring ESXi-aware encryption, VM hibernation bypass, and mandatory data exfiltration before encryption. LockBit 4.0 affiliates are linked to a disproportionate share of healthcare and critical infrastructure attacks in 2026.

name: BlackCat
description: BlackCat (ALPHV) operates the most technically sophisticated ransomware family, written in Rust for cross-platform targeting of Windows, Linux, and VMware ESXi. The group pioneered triple extortion (encryption + data leak + DDoS threat) and was among the first to target CI/CD pipelines. Despite an FBI-led disruption and seizure of infrastructure in December 2023, BlackCat/ALPHV affiliates reconstituted with hardened operations in 2025-2026 targeting energy and critical manufacturing.

name: Scattered Spider
description: Scattered Spider (UNC3944) is a loosely affiliated criminal collective believed to be composed primarily of English-speaking members in their teens and twenties. Despite limited technical background, the group demonstrates exceptional social engineering capabilities — bypassing MFA via fatigue attacks, SMS phishing, and service desk social engineering. They leverage legitimate remote administration tools and partner with established ransomware groups (ALPHV/BlackCat, RansomHub) to maximise impact. Responsible for major breaches at MGM Resorts ($100M+ loss), Caesars Entertainment, and numerous SaaS platforms.

name: Mustang Panda
description: Mustang Panda (Earth Preta/TA416) is a prolific Chinese APT with a long history of targeting government entities, NGOs, religious organisations, and think tanks in Southeast Asia, Europe, and the United States. The group is particularly active against targets related to Uyghur affairs, Taiwan, and South China Sea geopolitics. Known for PlugX malware and creative phishing using geopolitical lure documents, Mustang Panda typically achieves persistent access through spear-phishing and USB-based propagation.
